facts.value: Climber's path up the ridge to the first horn; downclimb a ~40-ft Class 3+ dihedral west, ledges to the notch, around the second horn's northeast side

evidence.fact: Path ends atop the first horn; an exposed Class 3+ dihedral of about 40 feet descends west to ledges and a notch.

facts.value: From the second horn, descend a ~150-ft Class 2-3 face into the deep notch, then ramps toward the summit horn

evidence.fact: A broken Class 2-3 face about 150 feet tall drops from the second horn into the deep notch.

facts.value: Class 4 / 5.0

evidence.fact: Summit horn: one full pitch, or two short ones, of Class 4 or 5.0 on the southeast ridge crest.
Final summit horn is one full pitch, or two short pitches, of roped climbing.

facts.value: Three bolts with large aluminum hangers on the summit pitch

evidence.fact: Three bolts with oversized aluminum hangers protect the summit-horn pitch.
Descent began with one 25-meter rappel from an established station down the upper ridge.
The single rappel down the upper ridge was 25 meters.

facts.value: Rappel the upper ridge, then reverse the route back through the notches

evidence.fact: After the rappel the party returned to Class 2 ledges and retraced the route from the deep notch.

facts.value: Highly exposed in places; two memorial plaques mark fatal falls

evidence.fact: Route is very exposed at several spots; plaques on ridge and summit honor climbers killed in falls.

wa_lundin_peak_southeast_ridge.note: Trailcatjim is one trip report (2023). SummitPost lists an 'East Ridge' route on Lundin, not used (different name).
